raw_response:
I am getting old now, so I do not want to toss things around too much. Stevia is what I know, and on only 5.5 mu I have to keep it steady. Last year if the seedlings took root well and the water followed in time, the leaves were decent, so this year I will still plant all 5.5 mu with stevia. I do not read those technical things, I just look at the soil, the苗情, and what people nearby do. Fertilizer costs money, water costs money, and there are only two of us at home, so I cannot manage it too finely. But I also do not dare use too little, because if the plants stay weak all season, then the whole year's income is thin. So I will use a moderate amount of fertilizer, put most of it on before or around transplanting, then add a bit later if the plants look pale. Since I have a well, I will irrigate when the field is dry, especially after transplanting and in the hot part of summer. Weeds and insects I will handle when I see them, not spray for nothing.
